title: Monotonic Array
statement: Decide whether the integer array `nums` only ever moves in one direction. Return `true` if, reading from left to right, its values never go down (each value is at least the one before it) **or** never go up (each value is at most the one before it); return `false` otherwise. Equal neighbours are allowed in both cases, so a constant array and a single value count as monotonic.
notes:
## Intuition

One way is to sort a copy both ways and see whether `nums` matches either, but that costs O(n log n). Instead, simulate one left-to-right walk and watch each neighbouring pair. A single step down rules out "never goes down"; a single step up rules out "never goes up". Keep one flag for each possibility and the array is monotonic if at least one flag survives the walk.

## Approach

1. Start with `increasing = true` and `decreasing = true`: nothing has disproved either yet.
2. For each index `i` from 1, compare `nums[i]` with `nums[i - 1]`.
3. If it is smaller, the array is not increasing: set `increasing = false`.
4. If it is larger, the array is not decreasing: set `decreasing = false`. Equal neighbours change nothing.
5. Return `increasing || decreasing`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 2, 3]`. At `i = 1`, `2 > 1`, so `decreasing = false`. At `i = 2`, `2 = 2`, so nothing changes. At `i = 3`, `3 > 2`, and `decreasing` stays `false`. `increasing` was never cleared, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the neighbouring pairs.
- Space: O(1): two flags.

## Pitfalls

- Use non-strict comparisons: `[2, 2]` is monotonic, so equal neighbours must not clear either flag.
- Do not decide the direction from just the first two values; with `[3, 3, 1]` the first pair is equal and gives no direction.
- An array of length 1 has no pairs, and both flags stay `true`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `increasing` | no step down has been seen so far |
| `decreasing` | no step up has been seen so far |
| `i` | index of the right value of the pair being compared |

narration.2: Assume the array never goes down until a step proves otherwise.
narration.3: Likewise assume it never goes up.
narration.5: Walk over every neighbouring pair, nums[i - 1] and nums[i].
narration.13: The array is monotonic if at least one direction was never broken.
